item.text: {"case_id":"SPR00041","decision":"candidate","candidate_ranking":["C25","C07","C11"],"selected_candidate_label":"C25","confidence":0.98,"relationship_type":"both","rationale":"C25 plausibly supplied a concrete drafting template. Both are 1951 proclamations enlarging national monuments under section 2 of the 1906 act; both distinguish federally held land that becomes part of the monument immediately from privately held land that will become part upon United States acquisition. They also share the same operative sequence: public-interest recitals, proclamation subject to existing rights, boundary description, warning clause, and National Park Service supervision clause. C07 and C11 are also strong monument-proclamation templates, but C25 contains the closest acquisition-contingent enlargement machinery.","shared_material":[{"child_excerpt":"do proclaim that, subject to all valid existing rights, the lands within the following-described boundaries which are now owned or controlled by the United States shall constitute the Muir Woods National Monument, and that ... [land] now owned by the William Kent Estate Company shall become a part of such monument upon the acquisition of title thereto or control thereof by the United States","parent_excerpt":"do proclaim that, subject to valid existing rights, the lands within the following-described areas in California owned by the United States are hereby added to and reserved as a part of the Lava Beds National Monument, and that the privately-owned lands within such areas shall become a part of such monument upon the acquisition of title thereto by the United States","explanation":"Distinctive parallel machinery makes current federal holdings part of the monument while conditionally incorporating private holdings upon later federal acquisition."},{"child_excerpt":"under and by virtue of the authority vested in me by section 2 of the act of June 8, 1906, 34 Stat. 225 (16 U.S.C. 431)","parent_excerpt":"under and by virtue of the authority vested in me by section 2 of the act of June 8, 1906, 34 Stat. 225 (16 U.S.C. 431)","explanation":"The identical authority clause supports the broader parallel operative structure, though it would not suffice alone."},{"child_excerpt":"Warning is hereby expressly given to all unauthorized persons not to appropriate, injure, destroy, or remove any feature of this monument and not to locate or settle upon any of the lands thereof. The Director of the National Park Service, under the direction of the Secretary of the Interior, shall have the supervision, management, and control","parent_excerpt":"Warning is hereby expressly given to all unauthorized persons not to appropriate, injure, destroy, deface, or remove any feature of this monument as hereby extended and not to settle upon any of the lands reserved as a part of this monument. The Director of the National Park Service, under the direction of the Secretary of the Interior, shall have the supervision, management, and control","explanation":"The matching warning and administrative provisions occur in the same post-description sequence and reinforce use of a common monument-enlargement template."}]}
